requirements.quote:
Each entry in the binders list is computed as an HMAC
   over a transcript hash (see Section 4.4.1) containing a partial
   ClientHello up to and including the PreSharedKeyExtension.identities
   field.
requirements.condition: when computing a PSK binder entry
requirements.required_behavior: compute it as an HMAC over a transcript hash
requirements.why_checkable: The binder algorithm and its transcript-hash input can be recomputed.

requirements.quote:
Each entry in the binders list is computed as an HMAC
   over a transcript hash (see Section 4.4.1) containing a partial
   ClientHello up to and including the PreSharedKeyExtension.identities
   field.
requirements.condition: when constructing the transcript input for a PSK binder
requirements.required_behavior: include the partial ClientHello through and including PreSharedKeyExtension.identities
requirements.forbidden_behavior: truncate the ClientHello before the end of PreSharedKeyExtension.identities
requirements.why_checkable: The exact transcript prefix boundary is identified by a parsed field.

requirements.quote:
That is, it includes all of the ClientHello but not the
   binders list itself.
requirements.condition: when constructing the transcript input for a PSK binder
requirements.required_behavior: include all ClientHello content other than the binders list
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include the binders list itself in the binder transcript
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized ClientHello can be truncated at the binders-list boundary and compared with the hashed input.

requirements.quote:
The length fields for the message (including
   the overall length, the length of the extensions block, and the
   length of the "pre_shared_key" extension) are all set as if binders
   of the correct lengths were present.
requirements.condition: when serializing the partial ClientHello used for binder computation
requirements.required_behavior: set the ClientHello overall length as if correctly sized binders were present
requirements.why_checkable: The synthetic overall length can be recomputed from the final binder sizes.

requirements.quote:
The length fields for the message (including
   the overall length, the length of the extensions block, and the
   length of the "pre_shared_key" extension) are all set as if binders
   of the correct lengths were present.
requirements.condition: when serializing the partial ClientHello used for binder computation
requirements.required_behavior: set the extensions-block length as if correctly sized binders were present
requirements.why_checkable: The synthetic extensions length can be recomputed from the final binder sizes.

requirements.quote:
The length fields for the message (including
   the overall length, the length of the extensions block, and the
   length of the "pre_shared_key" extension) are all set as if binders
   of the correct lengths were present.
requirements.condition: when serializing the partial ClientHello used for binder computation
requirements.required_behavior: set the pre_shared_key extension length as if correctly sized binders were present
requirements.why_checkable: The synthetic extension length can be recomputed from the final binder sizes.

requirements.quote:
The PskBinderEntry is computed in the same way as the Finished
   message (Section 4.4.4)
requirements.why_checkable: The binder computation can be compared with the implementation's Finished calculation.

requirements.quote:
but with the BaseKey being the binder_key
   derived via the key schedule from the corresponding PSK which is
   being offered (see Section 7.1).
requirements.condition: when computing a PskBinderEntry for an offered PSK
requirements.required_behavior: use as BaseKey the binder_key derived by the key schedule from that corresponding PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a binder_key derived from a different offered PSK
requirements.why_checkable: The PSK identity index and key-schedule input can be traced to the binder computation.

requirements.quote:
If the handshake includes a HelloRetryRequest, the initial
   ClientHello and HelloRetryRequest are included in the transcript
   along with the new ClientHello.
requirements.condition: when computing a binder after a HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: construct the transcript from the initial ClientHello, the HelloRetryRequest, and the new ClientHello in that order
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit or reorder any of those handshake messages
requirements.why_checkable: The binder transcript sequence can be compared with the recorded handshake messages.

requirements.quote:
if the client sends
   ClientHello1, its binder will be computed over:

      Transcript-Hash(Truncate(ClientHello1))
requirements.condition: when computing the binder in the initial ClientHello1
requirements.why_checkable: The formula identifies the exact sole transcript input for the first binder.

requirements.quote: Where Truncate() removes the binders list from the ClientHello.
requirements.condition: when applying Truncate to a ClientHello for binder computation
requirements.required_behavior: remove the binders list from the ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: retain the binders list in the truncated ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The truncation boundary is the parsed binders-list field.

requirements.quote:
If the server responds with a HelloRetryRequest and the client then
   sends ClientHello2, its binder will be computed over:

      Transcript-Hash(ClientHello1,
                      HelloRetryRequest,
                      Truncate(ClientHello2))
requirements.condition: when computing the binder in ClientHello2 after HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: compute it over Transcript-Hash(ClientHello1, HelloRetryRequest, Truncate(ClientHello2)) in that order
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit, reorder, or substitute any transcript component
requirements.why_checkable: The formula identifies the exact ordered transcript for the second binder.

requirements.quote:
The full ClientHello1/ClientHello2 is included in all other handshake
   hash computations.
requirements.condition: when performing a handshake hash computation other than PSK binder computation
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use Truncate(ClientHello1) in another handshake hash computation
requirements.why_checkable: Transcript construction for non-binder hashes can be checked for the complete first ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
The full ClientHello1/ClientHello2 is included in all other handshake
   hash computations.
requirements.condition: when performing a handshake hash computation other than PSK binder computation
requirements.required_behavior: include the full ClientHello2 when it exists
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use Truncate(ClientHello2) in another handshake hash computation
requirements.why_checkable: Transcript construction for non-binder hashes can be checked for the complete second ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
Note that in the first flight,
   Truncate(ClientHello1) is hashed directly
requirements.condition: when computing the binder transcript in the first flight
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reinject it as a message_hash handshake message
requirements.why_checkable: The first-flight transcript path can be checked for direct hashing of the truncated serialization.

requirements.quote:
but in the second flight,
   ClientHello1 is hashed and then reinjected as a "message_hash"
   message, as described in Section 4.4.1.
requirements.condition: when computing the binder transcript for ClientHello2 after HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: hash ClientHello1 and reinject that hash as a message_hash handshake message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: hash the serialized ClientHello1 directly in the second-flight transcript
requirements.why_checkable: The HelloRetryRequest transcript transform has a distinct synthetic message type and content.
